request.contents:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: The Landlord may increase the rent by up to the guideline amount once in any 12-month period by giving the Tenant 30 days' written notice.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
No, this clause is not enforceable. Under the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006*, a landlord cannot increase the rent without giving the tenant at least 90 days' written notice before the effective date of the increase (using the proper Landlord and Tenant Board form). Because this clause purports to allow a rent increase with only 30 days' notice, it conflicts with the statutory notice requirement and is void under section 4 of the Act.

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 116
